title: Signature Sandbox Provenance
description: Signature edition: every sandbox instance records its provenance — image hash, policy version, attestation, and what ran inside (hashes). The provenance answers 'what exactly executed this?' for every sandboxed run, making sandbox use auditable end to end. This is a Signature original method.
method: Record (image, policy, attestation, workload hashes) per instance; query during incidents; retain per policy.
usage: Log provenance automatically; consult it first in any sandbox-related incident.

demo.code:
print('sandbox #9912: image i7f2, policy p3, attested, ran job j8812')
print('incident: provenance shows exactly what executed')

title: Signature Attested sandbox launch
description: Signature edition: Before trusting a sandbox, attest it: measure its code and policy, verify the measurement, then provision secrets or sensitive work. The sandbox proves what it is before it's trusted with anything — attestation as the sandbox's birth certificate.
method: Measure sandbox image + policy; verify against allowlist; provision workload only on success; re-attest on update.
usage: Attest every sandbox before sensitive work; re-attest after any update.

demo.code:
print('sandbox measurement m7f2 verified against allowlist')
print('workload provisioned: sensitive batch job starts')

title: Signature Multi-party sandboxed computation
description: Signature edition: Parties contribute private inputs to a sandboxed joint computation: the sandbox runs under MPC or in a TEE, each party attests it, and the result is released only when all attestations verify. Nobody trusts anyone's machine — they trust the attested sandbox.
method: Deploy the computation in an attested sandbox/TEE; parties verify attestation; inputs contributed; result released on consensus.
usage: Use for joint computations among distrustful parties; verify attestations independently.

demo.code:
print('3 parties attest sandbox m7f2 -> all verify OK')
print('private inputs in; joint result out; no party saw others\' inputs')

title: Signature Egress-filtered crypto sandboxes
description: Signature edition: The sandbox's network is a cryptographic boundary: all egress through an encrypting proxy that only allows attested destinations, with payloads logged (in ciphertext) for audit. Data can't leave except through the approved, observed channel.
method: Proxy all egress; allowlist destinations; log encrypted payloads; block everything else by default.
usage: Default-deny egress; the allowlist is the security policy — review it.

demo.code:
print('egress attempt: api.vendor.com (allowlisted) -> PROXIED + logged')
print('egress attempt: evil.com -> DENIED (default)')

title: Signature Sandbox escape detection
description: Signature edition: Assume escape attempts: monitors watch for sandbox-boundary violations (unexpected syscalls, capability use anomalies, timing side channels) and kill the sandbox on detection. The sandbox is a containment that reports its own breaches — defense in depth around the boundary.
method: Monitor boundary crossings; anomaly-detect on syscall patterns; kill on violation; alert as security incident.
usage: Monitor every sandbox; treat escape attempts as incidents, not bugs.

demo.code:
print('sandbox attempted ptrace() (not in policy)')
print('KILLED + security incident opened')

title: Signature Compartmentalized crypto services
description: Signature edition: Split crypto services into compartments (key handling, protocol logic, I/O) with capabilities between them — a bug in the protocol parser can't reach the keys. Compartmentalization (CHERI, enclave-per-service) limits blast radius by architecture, enforced cryptographically.
method: Compartment per function; capabilities for inter-compartment calls; a compromised compartment can't escalate.
usage: Compartmentalize by privilege level; the key compartment should be tiny.

demo.code:
print('compartments: [parser] [protocol] [key-vault]')
print('parser exploited -> cannot reach key-vault (no capability)')

title: Signature Time-boxed cryptographic leases
description: Signature edition: Sandbox authority expires: capabilities and decryption keys carry leases, and when the lease lapses the sandbox loses access automatically — no revocation round-trip needed. Time-boxing bounds the damage of a compromised sandbox to the lease window.
method: Issue short-lived capabilities/keys; renew on health checks; expiry is automatic and total.
usage: Keep leases short; automate renewal; expiry must need no cooperation from the sandbox.

demo.code:
import time
lease_exp = time.time() + 300
print(f'capability lease expires in 300s')
print('compromised sandbox at 301s: authority GONE (no revocation needed)')

title: Signature Encrypted sandbox memory
description: Signature edition: The sandbox's memory is encrypted with keys the host doesn't hold (SEV-SNP, TDX): even a compromised hypervisor sees ciphertext. Cryptographic isolation at the hardware layer — the sandbox's thoughts are private even from the machine it runs on.
method: Run sandboxes under memory-encrypting TEEs; attest the TEE; the host handles scheduling, never plaintext.
usage: Use for sandboxes on untrusted infrastructure; verify attestation before scheduling.

demo.code:
print('sandbox under SEV-SNP: memory encrypted')
print('compromised hypervisor dump: ciphertext only')

title: Signature Proof-carrying sandbox policies
description: Signature edition: Sandbox policies (seccomp filters, capability sets) ship with proofs that they enforce the intended isolation: the policy is verified against a model of the kernel interface before installation. A misconfigured filter is caught by proof, not by exploit.
method: Model the policy; prove it denies the forbidden actions; install only proved policies; re-prove on change.
usage: Verify sandbox policies like code; the proof is the configuration review.

demo.code:
print('seccomp policy: 312 syscalls analyzed, 41 allowed')
print('proof: no allowed path to execve -> INSTALLED')
